semantics: A label with scored=false is out of contract. Its gold spans are removed from every gold count, and the bytes they cover (where no scored gold span also covers them) are ignored: they are neither leaked, nor true positive, nor false positive, nor counted as non-PII text. A prediction whose class is listed in neutral_prediction_classes is out of contract too: its bytes still count as protection where they cover scored gold, and are otherwise ignored rather than counted as false positive. Whether the pipeline still protected excluded gold is reported under excluded_label_coverage. Every corpus label must be listed; an unlisted label fails closed.

gold_gap.semantics: Gold-gap protection. The corpus labels a PII value where it is introduced and not always where it recurs. A predicted span is credited as gold-gap protection when (1) it overlaps no scored gold byte and no byte this contract ignores (excluded-label gold, neutral prediction classes); (2) after trimming ASCII whitespace at both ends its bytes are byte-identical to the value of a scored gold span in the same document, with no case folding, substring or lemmatisation; (3) its predicted class is listed against that gold label in compatible_labels; (4) neither neighbour of the trimmed span is a word character: a Unicode letter, digit or combining mark, a symbol Unicode names as a letter (circled A), or an unassigned code point. That set contains every code point Rust's char::is_alphanumeric accepts, so no credited edge is one Gaze's is_inside_word treats as inside a word. Only the trimmed bytes are credited; padding stays false positive. Credited bytes are reported in gold_gap_protected_bytes with a per-label breakdown, attributed to the first compatible gold span in document order, each byte once. This is a diagnostic beside the v2 numbers: leaked, true-positive and false-positive bytes and precision under utf8_bytes are computed exactly as in v2, and gold is never edited.
